title: Inter-Practice wire shapes (the inter-practice protocol PDR's clause 6; the PDR's number is estate-local)
$comment_contract: Core-carried: two estates validate inbound foreign material against the SAME document, so a mismatch is a typed refusal, never a silent misread. Version-family compatibility: within one MAJOR family evolution is additive-optional only — wire $defs deliberately tolerate unknown fields (additionalProperties true) so a newer minor parses under an older minor's validator, and every field added within a family MUST be optional so older payloads stay valid under newer validators. A breaking wire change is a MAJOR bump and a new family; cross-family contact is a typed refusal with an explicit version-mismatch message. Local estate schemas remain each estate's ENFORCEMENT surface (strict, additionalProperties false); this document is the CONTRACT for the wire-relevant subset, and each estate binds the two with a conformance test so drift red-gates.
$comment_scope: v1 floor: exactly the shapes the inter-practice protocol PDR's clause 6 names (the PDR's number is estate-local; each estate's own decision-record set carries it), as they exist on the live wire. The box-file exchange envelope is deliberately ABSENT: live box files are pin-free markdown prose by the clause-7 layering doctrine (concepts, no machine frontmatter), and their machine-readable time-bound layer IS the paired delivery comms event, covered by exchange_comms_event. Giving box files frontmatter would be new protocol surface — a family amendment, not a v1 recording.

wire_identity.$comment: The cross-estate identity tuple (clause 5): the session_id_prefix is the join key; names are repo-local derivations. Estates may attach local extras (deterministic ids, naming provenance) — wire readers tolerate them.

exchange_comms_event.$comment: The comms-event fields exchange relies on. required = what a foreign reader may rely on; optional = what it must tolerate. in_response_to is the comms-threading extension's field; audience/addressed_to carry directed routing.

claim_repo_ref.$comment: The repo-reference vocabulary (clause 1) as carried on claims — a version-advertised EXTENSION, not floor. origin is the durable coordinate (host/org/repo); machine-local checkout paths never travel.

watcher_heartbeat.$comment: A watcher is a writer (clause 4): its heartbeat is a wire surface a host estate's staleness consumers read. The founding 2026-07-05 refusal instance was a guest heartbeat under a host validator.

watcher_seen_file.$comment: The seen-file is TEXT, not JSON: newline-delimited event-id tokens. The event_id grammar is 'UUID or stable slug' (and ids are operator-overridable), so a line is any single whitespace-free token; CRLF is tolerated because the local readers split on \r?\n. An empty file means nothing seen yet; the final token's newline is optional; blank lines are refused.
